17 A projectile of mass 0.25 kg is at a height of 30 m above horizontal ground and travelling at a
speed of 15 m s–1. A short time later, it is at a height of 35 m above the horizontal ground and
travelling at a speed of 5.0 m s–1.
How much work is done against air resistance during this time?
A
0 J
B
13 J
C
25 J
D
37 J

hints: Notice both height and speed change: height rises from $30 \text{ m}$ to $35 \text{ m}$ while speed falls from $15 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ to $5.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, so calculate both $GPE = mgh$ and $KE = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$ at each point.
Connect the energies with conservation: without air resistance total $KE + GPE$ would stay constant, so work against resistance equals initial mechanical energy minus final mechanical energy.
Calculate the $KE$ loss of about $25 \text{ J}$ and the $GPE$ gain for $m = 0.25 \text{ kg}$ over $5 \text{ m}$, then subtract to find the net energy removed.
walkthrough: Find the initial mechanical energy at $30 \text{ m}$ with $v = 15 \text{ m s}^{-1}$: $KE_1 = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.25 \times 15^2 = 28.1 \text{ J}$ and $GPE_1 = 0.25 \times 9.81 \times 30 = 73.6 \text{ J}$, so total $E_1 \approx 101.7 \text{ J}$.

Find the final mechanical energy at $35 \text{ m}$ with $v = 5.0 \text{ m s}^{-1}$: $KE_2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.25 \times 5.0^2 = 3.1 \text{ J}$ and $GPE_2 = 0.25 \times 9.81 \times 35 = 85.8 \text{ J}$, so total $E_2 \approx 88.9 \text{ J}$.
Use the work-energy idea: work done against air resistance removes mechanical energy, so $W = E_1 - E_2$.
Substitute: $W \approx 101.7 - 88.9 = 12.8 \text{ J}$, about $13 \text{ J}$ after sensible rounding, with units in joules.

A.explanation: 0 J would mean total mechanical energy is conserved, but the calculated $KE + GPE$ decreases from about $102 \text{ J}$ to about $89 \text{ J}$.

B.explanation: The loss of total mechanical energy is about $12.7 \text{ J}$, which equals the work done against air resistance.

C.explanation: 25 J is only the loss of kinetic energy and ignores the $12.3 \text{ J}$ gain in gravitational potential energy as height rises from $30 \text{ m}$ to $35 \text{ m}$.

D.explanation: 37 J adds the kinetic energy loss to the potential energy gain instead of finding net change in $KE + GPE$.
